attribution_limitations: Table 1 uses one combined Negative/Normal column without values or reference ranges (colon transit 28.8 h is the only printed value). Flags were set only where one reading applies to the test type (negative for celiac and Yersinia serology; normal for quantitative, imaging and manometry rows); footnoted-exception rows and the composite urinary and gynecological rows keep flag unknown. The footnote symbol ∫ is printed for both laparoscopy and the lactulose breath test; content (hernia vs hydrogen/methane) was used to assign each footnote.

The same footnote symbol is attached to colonoscopy and abdominal-pelvic CT; the 4-cm jejunal tissue density is the narrative emergency CT finding (Table 1 CT row merged into that CT fact) and colonic coprostasis is not assignable to either exam. Table 1 records the CT as Negative/Normal although the footnote and narrative describe the jejunal mass.
Anorectal high-definition manometry is listed with both result columns blank; no result is inferred.

C. jejuni was PCR positive but antigen negative and "considered a colonizer"; no enteric infection is inferred. The positive lactulose breath test (hydrogen peak and methane at least 20 ppm) carries no stated SIBO diagnosis. A gastric biopsy microfocus of intestinal metaplasia is described only as a gastroscopy exception.

FMT regimen: the capsule description (20 capsules within an hour on two separate days per treatment) may be the general protocol; per-day versus total count is not clear in text. Figure 1 pixels show two capsule icons per FMT on two dates (legend "FMT treatment 20 capsules"), consistent with 20 capsules per day but not stated in text. The vancomycin/bowel-cleansing timing relative to each FMT is also not clear.

The abstract and text say symptoms remained better after a year with only the burning sensation persisting, while the discussion says "remission of gastrointestinal symptoms 1 y after FMT". Do not treat the burning sensation as resolved or all symptoms as remitted.

The discussion says the patient "exhibited gut inflammation" with no objective support while Table 1 lists inflammatory markers and fecal calprotectin as Negative/Normal; retained as a review-only statement. The sentence about loose stools "observed following FMT pretreatment" is not assigned to the patient because ownership is unclear.

Text/figure disagreements found on pixel inspection (not text-only facts): the text says patient-specific core genera fell to less than 3% at 6 months post-FMT, but Figure 2C prints 3.381 for the Pre-FMT/M1/M4/M6 core at M6; and the text says environmentally acquired strains averaged 11.5% post-FMT, but Figure 2C acquisition rows sum to far less. Figure 2A y-axis reads species level while the caption says ASV level. Lachnospira is named as boosted by FMT in the text but is not green-colored in Figure 3 (two-fold rule).
The healthy 32-year-old male donor (Caucasian, BMI 25.5 kg/m2, nonsmoker, no medication) is background; none of these attributes belongs to the recipient and the donor is not a second index patient.

claims.text: With IBS-SSS above 300 and a high quality-of-life burden, a multidisciplinary meeting proposed three experimental oral FMTs, given from the same donor after 5 days of vancomycin and bowel cleansing.
